newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cabinet discusses social security finance.
newsitem.headline: French cabinet discusses social security finance.

text.p: The French government on Wednesday discussed the 1997 financing plan for the country's social security system, which remains deep in the red less than a year after a big debt write-off.
"It's a first and it's one of the strong points of the reform of the social security system started a year ago," budget minister Alain Lamassoure said after the cabinet meeting.

He said Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot told the meeting that during 1996, the social security deficit would be cut by 15 billion French francs ($2.90 billion) from the 1995 level, a result which he called "positive" although it was below the planned level.
"The financing plan has been drawn up around the aim to bring back the social security deficit from over 50 billion francs to a bit below 30 billion -- 29.7 billion -- in 1997," Lamassoure said.
He quoted Juppe as telling the ministers that the reform "was the final chance to save the French social security system."
